subject: science
passage: A sample of uranium-238 loses half of its atoms to radioactive decay in about 4.5 billion years, a figure so reliable that geologists use it to date some of the oldest rocks on Earth. That regularity, however, describes only the aggregate. For any single nucleus, decay is ______: physics can state the likelihood that the atom will decay within a given interval but cannot, even in principle, specify when it will do so, and a nucleus that has already survived for billions of years is no more "due" to decay than one formed yesterday.
stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?

explanation.why: "However" contrasts the reliable behavior of a whole sample with the behavior of one nucleus. The colon defines the blank: physics can give only "the likelihood" of decay, never the moment. The word must mean "governed by chance and describable only in terms of likelihood."
explanation.A: Incorrect. "Deterministic" means fixed in advance by prior conditions. The regularity of a large sample might suggest this, but the text says the timing for one nucleus cannot be specified "even in principle."
explanation.B: Correct. "Probabilistic" means describable only in terms of probability, which fits decay whose likelihood can be stated but whose timing cannot.
explanation.C: Incorrect. "Cyclical" means repeating in a regular cycle, but a nucleus decays once, and the text says its age does not make decay any more "due."
explanation.D: Incorrect. "Imminent" means about to happen, but a single nucleus may survive for billions of years; the text stresses that its timing is unknown.
